items.text: In the ruler your father's presence, do not wear the jade pendant; tie it up on the left.
items.citation: Liji, Yu Zao II.17 … Yu Zao III.7
items.quote: When the ruler was present, (his son and heir) did not wear the pendant of jade-stones. He tied it up on the left of his girdle

items.text: Dress in the manner proper to your husband's rank.
items.citation: Liji, Yu Zao II.17 … Yu Zao III.7
items.quote: The others all wore the dresses proper to them as the wives of their husbands.

items.text: Do not dress your hair in tufts after your parents are dead.
items.quote: When his parents were dead, (a son) did not have his hair dressed in tufts (any more).

items.text: Wear the white silk cap with dark border while mourning (and for a grandson as well).
items.quote: A cap of white silk with the border or roll of a dark colour was worn (? at his capping) by a son or grandson (when in a certain stage of mourning).

items.text: Obey your father's summons at once, laying aside your work and hurrying to him, not even finishing your mouthful.
items.quote: a son reverently obeyed it without any delay. Whatever work he had in hand, he laid aside. He ejected the meat that was in his mouth, and ran

items.text: When your parents are old and you are away, do not go elsewhere or delay your return; show distress in your face when they are ill.
items.quote: When his parents were old and he had gone away, he did not go to a second place, nor delay his return beyond the time agreed on; when they were ailing, his looks and manner appeared troubled

items.text: After your father's death, do not read his books, for his hand's touch seems still upon them.
items.quote: When his father died, he could not (bear to) read his books;--the touch of his hand seemed still to be on them.

items.text: After your mother's death, do not drink from the cups and bowls she used, for her breath's touch seems still upon them.
items.quote: When his mother died, he could not (bear to) drink from the cups and bowls that she had used;--the breath of her mouth seemed still to be on them.

items.text: When you exchange courtesies or receive gifts while your father is alive, credit him and appeal to his authority.
items.quote: if his father were alive, he would appeal to his authority; if the other gave him a gift, he would say, in making obeisance for it, that he did so for his father.

items.text: When eating with someone older or higher in rank, be the last to put down the offering and the first to taste the food.
items.quote: When one was sitting at a meal with another older than himself, or of a different (and higher) rank, he was the last to put down the offering', but the first to taste the food.
